title: Capacity Sprint Signalboard — regional shifts & prewarm notes
body:
Purpose:
- Quick-sync signalboard for the ongoing capacity sprint. Captures regional demand shifts, prewarm experiment notes, temporary routing adjustments, and immediate action items for the next 72 hours.
- Audience: infra oncall, SREs, serving-runtime leads, product owners (hosted API), solutions engineering.

Executive summary:
- APAC surge: Singapore + Sydney experienced a sustained QPS uplift beginning 2026-05-30 (~30-40% above two-week baseline).
- Capacity posture: West US + EU show spare capacity (~12% combined), APAC p100/p40 latency pools at ~96% utilization for priority traffic.
- Prewarm experiment #3 (dynamic prewarm, 90s warm window) materially reduced cold-start tail latency (~45% median tail reduction) at ~8% short-term GPU usage increase on test pools.
- Short-term mitigations: route 18% of non-geo-restricted low-latency requests to EU canary, enable aggressive prefix/KV cache sharing in SG A/B cohort, and temporarily bump APAC burst triggers by +2 nodes during peak windows.

Observed signals (last 72h):
- APAC (SG+SYD): QPS +32% vs baseline. Completion p99 increased 430ms -> 920ms during local peak windows.
- West US: steady; 95th latency flat; spare capacity ~12% across mixed pools.
- EU (FRA/NL): utilization +9%; viable overflow region for canary routing.
- Prewarm #3 A/B: ~21k requests over 48h. Cold-start p99 improved from 1.3s to 0.72s for prewarmed instances. Token throughput unchanged. Incremental GPU-hours +8% in test pool.
- Incident notes: autoscaler flapping in SG traced to healthcheck TTL misconfig (INFRA-2143); rollback applied 2026-06-01 14:12 UTC.

Key meeting notes: 2026-06-01 standup
- Decision to run EU blended routing canary (18%) for non-geo traffic. Lucas to own rollout and rollback criteria.
- Retro highlight: product should provide a "reservation hint" tag for enterprise customers to distinguish reserved vs burst traffic.
- Prewarm policy: product to confirm acceptable incremental cost threshold (discussed threshold <=10% for ~40% tail reduction) by EOD 2026-06-05.

Actions in flight:
- Lucas Moreno — roll out 18% blended routing to EU for non-geo traffic; monitor latency per 5m windows — ETA: 2026-06-02 23:00 UTC.
- Jin Park — adjust autoscaler TTLs and healthcheck config to prevent SG flapping (follow-up INFRA-2143) — ETA: 2026-06-03 04:00 UTC.
- Ethan Carter — enable cross-region KV prefix-cache sharing prototype on serving-runtime; gather hit-rate and latency delta — ETA: 2026-06-05.
- Anika Shah — compile enterprise reservation list and tagging schema for reservation hints — ETA: 2026-06-04 18:00 UTC.
- Priya Nambiar — approve temporary +2 burst nodes in APAC for 48h and confirm billing owner for spike — ETA: 2026-06-02 18:00 UTC (in-progress).

Risks / concerns:
- Cross-region routing increases egress and may violate egress-related SLA clauses for some reserved customers; legal/finance review required if exceeded.
- Prewarm costs scale non-linearly; full-region rollout could push short-window GPU costs to +20-25% without further optimizations.
- Autoscaler config remains sensitive; aggressive TTLs could reintroduce flapping. Need extended soak and additional canary nodes in SG.

Temporary config changes applied:
- 2026-06-02 16:20 UTC — APAC burst-capacity trigger increased from 4 -> 6 nodes for p40-latency pool (1h rollback guard).
- 2026-06-02 19:40 UTC — KV-cache sharing flag enabled experimental on serving-runtime v3.2-stable in SG A/B cohort.

Telemetry & dashboards to watch:
- infra:gpu-utilization-by-region (5m), infra:latency-p99-by-endpoint (1m), infra:prewarm-cost-projection (1h).
- product:customer-reservation-usage (daily).
- Alerts: #infra-apac-high-util Slack channel.

Decision log:
- 2026-06-01 17:10 UTC — Priya + SRE leads approved 18% EU blend canary.
- Wider prewarm rollout deferred pending product cost threshold confirmation.

Open questions:
- Is 18% the optimal canary percentage? Suggest evaluate 10% (conservative) -> 20% (faster).
- Should reservation hints be surfaced automatically from hosted-api billing events or require manual tagging by account teams?
- If prewarm approved, what warm window is acceptable at scale (30s, 60s, 90s, 3m)? Experiment #3 used 90s; product may request 60s.

Next checkpoints:
- Quick check: 2026-06-02 23:15 UTC (1h post-canary) — Lucas report.
- Deep dive: 2026-06-03 15:00 UTC — prewarm results + cost projection.
- Sprint demo: 2026-06-07 10:00 UTC — infra + product + solutions present recommended permanent controls.

Runbook snippets (short):
- If APAC p99 > 1.2s for >10m: (1) enable EU blend, (2) notify #infra-apac-high-util, (3) open incident stub with INFRA-PRIO tag.
- Canary rollback criteria: global p99 increase >10% or error rate >0.5% absolute over baseline for 5m.

Notes-to-self / informal:
- Confirm finance breakdown for prewarm overhead (hourly by pool). Current billing view lumps prewarm into burst costs.
- Discuss sanitized customer-to-reservation mapping with CS for internal use.
